newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa bounces from lows as NY surges.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa bounces from lows as NY surges.

text.p: Cocoa futures bounced from four-month lows this morning to end Thursday mixed with nearby months posting slight gains on short-covering after a better-than-expected performance in New York.
Trading was quite volatile. London's September hit a new low of 965 stg this morning as specs unloaded their long positions.
But after New York bucked its sharply lower opening call to push higher at the outset, shorts returned to cover positions and lifted September by 20 stg.
The contract closed just one stg up at 987 stg a tonne.
December was three up at 1,020 but distant May fell 11 at 1,046.
New York's September stood $15 higher at $1,512 a tonne at 1623 GMT.
Traders said while some buyers might be enticed at current levels, the bounce did not justify the weak fundamental picture.
"The prices may be cheap but there are no (fundamental) reasons for the market to move up," said one.

Volume of 9,415 lots were made up mainly of Sept/Dec switches which traded at around 33 stg. For the last three days, the spread moved within 31 and 39 stg, with keen sellers seen at 31 and buyers at 39.
Technically, the market's downside potential seemed limited after today's successful break below the previous 968 stg support.
The next key support is seen at 950.

Broker GNI said Wednesday's news on trade expectations of higher Ivorian cocoa farmgate prices for next season could be viewed as a short-term positive factor as it would encourage holding over a larger portion of the mid-crop to mix with the new season's main-crop beans.

Among latest news, the effect on cocoa volumes of Ivory Coast's policy of evicting farmers from illegal forest encampments could be offset by better husbandry and replanting elsewhere, donor sources said.
